subject.title: macOS update can leave manual-update loop and stale node host causing Gateway restart storm

question: Should this issue remain the canonical tracker for the combined macOS updater-loop failure, or should maintainers split the remaining work into narrower launchd job cleanup, no-op update policy, and node-host recovery items?
rationale: Current main has partial repairs, but the remaining behavior crosses update policy, launchd label matching, and live macOS proof requirements; automation should not choose the product boundary or cleanup scope alone.

options.title: Keep this canonical
options.body: Use this issue to track the remaining macOS updater-loop fix and require real LaunchAgent update proof before closure.

options.title: Split and cross-link
options.body: Create narrower maintainer-owned items for `manualupdate` stale-job cleanup, same-version update/dedupe policy, and node-host recovery, then close this only after those references are canonical.

options.title: Close only after live proof
options.body: If a maintainer runs a current-main macOS npm-global LaunchAgent update/no-op smoke and proves no loop or stale node-host state, close as implemented with that evidence.

recommendation.title: Keep this canonical
recommendation.body: Use this issue to track the remaining macOS updater-loop fix and require real LaunchAgent update proof before closure.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent supplied the closest maintainer-side close-condition signal for the related macOS LaunchAgent update family and is already tied to release/update recovery history.
